steps.text: The cosine argument increases by $2\pi$, leaving the seasonal value unchanged.

The seasonal term can raise or lower the total by up to 6 degrees, so actual threshold crossings differ.

stem: Demand at price $p$ is $q(p)=200-6p$ for $10\le p\le30$. A discount policy maps the listed price $x$ to $p=0.8x+2$. Listed prices must keep the actual price in the demand model’s domain. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find demand as a function of listed price and determine its valid domain.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write revenue as a function of listed price, then determine the listed price giving maximum revenue.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why using $xq(x)$ would be an incorrect revenue calculation.

steps.text: Its vertex corresponds to actual price $p=200/12=50/3$.
Customers pay the discounted price $0.8x+2$, not the listed price x.
The demand input must also be the actual price, requiring the composition.

title: An average-cost inverse and a feasibility limit
stem: Total cost for $q>0$ units is $C(q)=500+8q$, giving average cost $A(q)=C(q)/q$. A manager wants an average cost no greater than 9 per unit. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find $A^{-1}$ and state its physically relevant domain.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the least integer production meeting the target.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The factory can make at most 420 units. Find its lowest possible average cost and assess a promise of average cost 8.

steps.text: A decreases as positive q increases, so use $q=420$.
Average cost 8 cannot be reached at any finite positive q; 8 is a limiting value.

title: A growth claim with two intersections
stem: Two forecasts are $E(t)=20e^{0.2t}$ and $L(t)=20+10t$ for $0\le t\le12$. Both start at the same value. A report says the exponential forecast is larger at every positive time because exponentials grow faster than linear functions. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the second intersection and determine where each forecast is larger.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Use the initial rates of change to explain the report’s error.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find when the two instantaneous growth rates are equal.

steps.text: Solve $20e^{0.2t}=20+10t$ numerically, retaining the known root $t=0$.
L is larger between 0 and the second root; E is larger afterwards.
Initially the linear forecast increases at 10, while E increases at only 4.
Faster eventual growth does not imply a larger value at every positive time.

title: A parameter that changes the number of feasible solutions
stem: An introduced model is $f_k(x)=x^2-4x+k$ on the physically allowed domain $x\ge0$. A zero represents a break-even production level. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Classify the number of distinct non-negative zeros as k varies.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find k if the two feasible break-even levels differ by 6.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the greatest possible separation between two feasible zeros.

steps.text: For $k<0$: only the positive root is feasible.
But k=-5 gives roots -1 and 5, so there cannot be two feasible levels separated by 6.
No admissible k satisfies the stated condition.
The greatest separation is 4 at $k=0$, with roots 0 and 4.

title: A sensor response that approaches a moving target
stem: A response is modelled by the introduced function $S(t)=\ln(1+e^t)$ for $t\ge0$. A simpler approximation is $L(t)=t$. The diagram shows the two predictions. Give non-exact numerical answers to three significant figures unless stated otherwise.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that the approximation error is $E(t)=\ln(1+e^{-t})$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the least t for which the approximation error is at most 0.01.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain whether the approximation overestimates or underestimates S, and what happens to the error for large t.

steps.text: Taking logarithms and subtracting t gives $E(t)=\ln(1+e^{-t})$.
The error is positive, so L underestimates S.
Since $e^{-t}\to0$, the error tends to zero.
